title: When Is the Best Time to Buy a New HVAC System?
h1: When Is the Best Time of Year to Buy a New HVAC System?
description: Spring and fall are usually the best times to buy a new HVAC system. Here's why off-peak timing helps with scheduling, options and avoiding a rushed decision.
quick_answer: The best time to buy a new HVAC system is usually spring or fall, when demand is lower and you aren't relying on heating or cooling every day. Installers have more open schedules, you have time to compare options and you avoid replacing a failed system in a rush during a heat wave or cold snap.
body:
In Southern California, the busiest stretches for HVAC companies are hot spells in late summer and early fall and the first cold nights of winter. If you can plan your replacement around those, you'll have a smoother experience.

Why are spring and fall the best times?

Off-peak months give you a few real advantages:

  • Scheduling. Installers aren't stacked up with emergency calls, so you can usually pick a date that works for you.
  • Time to compare. You can get a proper load calculation, look at a few options and think it over without sweating in a 90-degree house.
  • Comfortable install days. Working in an attic is much easier in mild weather, and you won't miss your AC or heat for the day or two of the install.
  • Promotions. Manufacturers and contractors often run offers during slower months. Check our specials page for anything current.

Is it better to replace before the system fails?

Almost always. When a system dies in the middle of a heat wave, you're stuck choosing from whatever is in stock and whoever can come soonest. Planning ahead lets you choose the right equipment, fix ductwork at the same time and budget for it.

Signs it's time to start planning:

  • The AC or heat pump is 12 or more years old, or the furnace is past 15
  • You've needed more than one significant repair in the past couple of years
  • The system uses R-22 refrigerant
  • Energy bills are climbing and comfort is slipping
  • Your technician has flagged a worn compressor, leaking coil or cracked heat exchanger

Does the timing differ for coastal and inland homes?

A little. Near the coast, the AC may only run on warm afternoons, so there's more flexibility. Late winter or spring works well. Inland neighborhoods that get hot summers should aim to replace cooling equipment in spring, before the heat sets in.

For heating, early fall is ideal. Inland valleys and foothill areas can get cold at night, and you want a working furnace or heat pump before the first chilly week. Fall is also when Santa Ana winds and wildfire smoke can show up, so it's a good time to think about filtration as part of the new system.

Are there other good times to replace a system?

  • During a remodel or addition. If walls and ceilings are open, upgrading ducts and equipment together saves work.
  • When you buy a home. An inspection may show an old system that's worth replacing before you move in.
  • When incentives are available. Utility and state rebates for efficient equipment, especially heat pumps, come and go. Ask about what applies when you get your quote.
  • When you're adding a room or converting a garage. That's a good time to look at zoning or a ductless mini-split.

What happens if your system fails in peak season?

It happens, and it's not the end of the world. A technician can often make a repair that buys you time, even if replacement is the long-term answer. That gives you a few weeks to compare options instead of signing the first quote you get on a hot afternoon.

If the repair isn't safe or practical, such as a furnace with a cracked heat exchanger, ask about temporary options like portable heaters or a window unit while the new system is scheduled. Never keep running a furnace that a technician has flagged as unsafe.

How should you prepare for a replacement?

  1. Write down any comfort problems, like hot upstairs rooms or noisy vents.
  2. Gather recent energy bills if you want to compare efficiency options.
  3. Get a load calculation instead of simply matching the old unit's size.
  4. Ask that the ducts be inspected, since leaky or crushed ducts will hold back a new system.
  5. Review warranty terms and maintenance requirements in writing.

When you're ready, our HVAC replacement team will come out, look at the whole system and give you a free estimate with a few options to choose from.
faqs: How long does a new HVAC installation take?

A straightforward replacement of a furnace and AC often takes one to two days. Adding new ductwork, moving equipment or running new electrical can add time. Your installer should give you a schedule before work starts.
Is it worth waiting for a sale to replace my system?

Only if your current system is still working safely. If it has failed, or there's a safety concern with a furnace, don't wait. If it's running fine but aging, planning a replacement during a slower month is a smart move.
Can I replace just the outdoor unit?
Sometimes, but it's often not recommended. Indoor and outdoor components are designed to work as a matched set. Mismatched equipment can lose efficiency and may affect the warranty.
